verdict: Lend selectively to Namakkal layer farms with owned sheds, NECC-linked offtake and tight feed cover; avoid thin-net-worth partnership units and broiler-only exposures until feed and price data are verified.
title: Namakkal Poultry Farming: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What this business physically is
Namakkal is a layer cluster: about 1,100 farms and roughly 4 crore layer birds producing near 3 crore eggs a day [1], with industry estimates of 5–6 crore eggs a day rising to about 8 crore in peak season [3]. **The unit of credit is the shed-and-bird cycle, not the farm gate.** Birds eat maize and soya meal trucked in from other states [3]; eggs move out daily to Kerala, Karnataka and Gulf export markets [3]. Cash comes in daily, cost sits in feed bought weekly, and the spread is set by the NECC Namakkal benchmark price [3].

## Where value and cash sit now
Procurement price was fixed at Rs.6.20, up from Rs.6.10 the previous day [1]. **A one-day move of this size tells you the farmer has almost no pricing power — the benchmark passes feed and demand swings straight through** [3]. Feed is the swing cost: Q2 FY27 at SKM Egg saw EBITDA fall to Rs.28 crore from Rs.38 crore on higher feed raw material cost [7], while Venky's Q3 FY26 profit more than doubled on cheaper feed [5][6]. So when a proposal lands, check the feed purchase ledger and the last six NECC price prints together; if feed cost rose while the NECC price fell, ask for the margin per egg and the number of birds in lay.

## The growth opportunity
**Pursue layer farms that own their sheds and have added feed milling, tray supply or transport** — the cluster has built these around the farms [3], and integrated players carry a competitive edge over unorganised units [10]. Also pursue table-egg exporters with Gulf offtake [3]. Avoid broiler-only units: Q4 FY26 broiler realisation peaked at INR 102.67/kg, April FY27 at INR 97–100/kg, and DOC prices fell from about INR 55 to INR 21–22 in parts of North India by mid-May [4] — that is a falling market, not a lending case. Avoid thin partnership firms: Sree Renuka Poultry had net worth of Rs.12.25 crore as of March 31, 2024, with capital withdrawal and dissolution risk [11].

## How to grow safely
Structure against the daily cash cycle: **charge the egg sale proceeds account, take weekly stock-and-mortality statements, and take the NECC price sheet every month.** Watch liquidity, not just profit — Srinivasa Farms ran a current ratio of 1.08x but a quick ratio of 0.45x as on March 31, 2026, with cash flow from operations negative at Rs.28 crore and bank limits of Rs.25 crore utilised around 89% [8]. So if a borrower's quick ratio sits near 0.45x, ask for the feed creditor ageing and promoter infusion record before enhancing limits.

## Early-warning signs
- Weekly: laying percentage or bird mortality moves beyond the borrower's own trailing norm -> ask for the vet report and biosecurity spend; bird flu would hit exports [3].
- Monthly: NECC Namakkal price falls while maize cost rises [1][3] -> cut drawing power and ask for the margin per egg.
- Monthly: egg sale proceeds routed away from the charged account -> treat as diversion and freeze enhancement.
- Quarterly: bank limit utilisation crosses 89% with negative cash flow from operations [8] -> move to stock statement plus receivables review.

Namakkal-specific published data is thin beyond the price and bird counts [1][3]; the rating reports [8][11] are undated and the peer results are national, so lean on first principles and collect from customer the district-level feed cost, laying rate and shed capex.
